candidate.answerReason: A lies on the major arc BD and therefore intercepts the 140-degree minor arc. Thus A is 70 degrees and its opposite angle C is 110 degrees.

methods.label: Find A and use opposite angles
methods.explanation: \(\angle A=\angle BOD\div 2=70^\circ\). Opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary, so \(\angle C=180^\circ-70^\circ=110^\circ\).

methods.label: Use the major arc directly
methods.explanation:
The opposite vertices \(A\) and \(C\) lie on opposite arcs with endpoints \(B,D\). Since \(A\) lies on the major arc \(BD\), \(C\) lies on the minor arc, so \(\angle C\) intercepts the major arc. This arc measures \(360^\circ-140^\circ=220^\circ\). By the inscribed angle theorem,
\[
\angle C=\frac{220^\circ}{2}=110^\circ.
\]
methods.levelReason: Uses the same Grade 9 inscribed angle theorem with full-circle angle arithmetic.

candidate.annotationRationale:
The route-neutral target is determining an inscribed angle from the central angle and arc location, covered by cnm_253. The first method additionally uses cnm_255 and supplementary-angle knowledge. The alternative computes the intercepted major arc directly. Circle and arc concepts and elementary angle operations support both methods.
